messages:
sophia: Proposal — make routing policy pluggable per-tenant + add a short 'residency grace window' at the proxy layer so transient region mismatches don't hard-fail production traffic. Rough sketch: config endpoints, enforcement flag, two-phase fallback (soft then hard), and metrics. Thoughts?
kevin: +1 on pluggable. Default should be simple: prefer resident region, soft-fallback to nearest on transient errors. Suggest default grace_window = 30s. Main runtime worry is KV-cache ownership TTLs and inflight requests.
dennis: Operator perspective: 30s feels tight for drain scenarios. IRL drain + jitter + routing convergence can be ~60s. Suggest 60s soft window + extra 30s for stagger = 90s total tolerance, or two-phase: soft-fallback (60s) then hard-fail after another 30s. Also want an operator override to force fallback during maintenance. :thinking:
raj: Legal constraint: EU-residency tenants must not have writes routed outside EU unless explicit consent. Reads from cache or read-only replicas are ok. We need a per-tenant flag `residency_enforced` and explicit consent header when overriding: `X-Redwood-Consent: eu-data-allowed`. If enforced=true => block write fallback entirely.
sophia: Example request header we'd honor: `X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1` and optional consent header. Inline example: `POST /v1/generate`
`X-Redwood-Region: eu-west-1`
`X-Redwood-Consent: eu-data-allowed`
If consent missing and tenant.enforced => 403 from proxy.
kevin: From runtime: easy to check headers/tenant flag and route. Need to attach metric tags like `route_policy=soft_fallback|blocked|hard_fallback` and `routed_region=eu-west-1|us-west-2`. Also we should emit the reason for fallback in traces so SRE can triage. For KV-caches, when we soft-fallback we must avoid expiring local ownership immediately — otherwise we risk split-brain cache writes.
priya: Quick question — increasing grace window will keep more traffic in the resident path during flaps, but does that increase cold-cache miss rate in fallback region when we do flip? What's the perf cost?
kevin: Good point. Tradeoff: longer grace reduces wrong-region routing but increases chance of tail latency spikes for requests that wait for resident. If we soft-fallback to nearest (read-only) for reads, we can reduce user-visible latency. For writes with enforcement=false we can queue short window then fallback. For enforcement=true we must return error. Recommend experiment to measure 50/60/90s.
dennis: Proposed operator metrics: `grace_window_enter_ts`, `grace_window_exit_ts`, `fallback_count_by_tenant`, `blocked_write_count_by_reason`. Add an emergency operator flag: `region.force_fallback=true` that overrides tenant soft-fallbacks for planned maintenance. :+1:
deploy-bot: Feature flag `pluggable-region-policy` toggled ON in staging (canary 10% traffic).
sophia: Plan: I'll open a follow-up RFC with: config surface (per-tenant flag + global defaults), proxy behavior (soft-window timeline, metrics, consent header), operator overrides, and a short experiment matrix (gracewindows=30/45/60, 10 tenants, EU-enforced toggles). Anyone want to pair on the experiment design?
kevin: I can help with the runtime experiment harness and add trace tags.
raj: I'll provide a checklist for legal gating and what counts as consent.
dennis: I'll sketch the operator runbook for maintenance + emergency override.
sophia: Great — creating the RFC doc now and adding links to the staging canary results. Will ping when ready. :rocket:
